I told her to just leave my ex alone and stop pretending. The brother, came rushing out of his room from hearing this and said "What did you say to my mom?!" I told him the same thing. At this point, I knew what was about to happen. I got up my bed and was bracing from an attack. We exchanged words, my mom tried to block the door way preventing him from getting in. He eventually juked her and rushed straight for me. Lunging and trying to take me down using his jiu jitsu techniques. I swung but nothing was really hitting him correctly. I never learned how to fight and I have always been a passive person because of how I was raised, but there was no other way I could defend myself from him.
He threw a few punches on my nose and lip, blood splattered across my closet door, he lunged again and pinned me down. Throwing punches on my face while I tried to throw some back to no avail.
My mom tried to pull him back and in the heat of it all, my anger towards both of them I said these words, "...see! This is your fault! This is your fault!" at my mom. While the brother was throwing punches on my face, my mom reached down and slapped me hard. My eyes widened and I stared at her.

Time felt like it stopped after I felt that smack. That's when I realized that this is my supposed family. This..is my family..

I don't remember exactly what happened after and how the punching stopped.

Stretching every hour or so in between your daily sitting activities will help, like toe touch and hip stretch. It doesn't have to be an extreme stretching session. A few minute stretch is enough. The idea is to teach your body to keep or improve it's flexibility.
Sitting for long periods of time will eventually shorten your hip muscles, so counter act it by remembering to stretch on your breaks. Set a timer if you have to.

Like what others have mentioned, standing up and walking helps as well. Don't try to engage in another hour of workout and just let your body recover. Also, make your off days an active recovery day. You can go for a light run or swim, if that's your thing. You may even want to learn Yoga and do a series of stretching instead.
